description: The file-control COLLATING SEQUENCE clause (ISO 12.4.5.7) - the collating sequence for the record keys of an INDEXED file (Format 1 file-level IS/FOR ALPHANUMERIC/FOR NATIONAL, Format 2 key-level OF key... IS alphabet). A COBOL-2002 introduction (programmable indexed-key collating); 0900 below 2002. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): the ANSI X3.23-1985 indexed file control entry ends `RECORD KEY IS data-name-1 [ ALTERNATE RECORD KEY IS data-name-2 [ WITH DUPLICATES ] ] … [ FILE STATUS IS data-name-3 ] .` (§1985:IX.2.3.2), and §1985:IX.2.3.4 GR3 fixes the key order: 'For an indexed file, the collating sequence associated with the native character set is assumed'; §2002:12.3.4.6 introduces the clause: 'The COLLATING SEQUENCE clause specifies the collating sequence to be used for the ordering of record keys and alternate record keys for an indexed file' (§2002:12.3.4.6.3 GR1: 'Each collating sequence is a fixed file attribute'). §2002:F.2 has no item that names the clause; its item 24 records the change it belongs to: 'For each use of a collating sequence, language is provided for specifying either an alphanumeric collating sequence or a national collating sequence, or both.' §2014:12.4.4.6 carries the 2002 sentence unchanged, so 2014 = 2023. Parses at all editions (superset), introduction-gated post-bind by VersionConformancePass.

IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. ROWCOL.
       ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
       CONFIGURATION SECTION.
       SPECIAL-NAMES.
           ALPHABET AL IS "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ".
       INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION.
       FILE-CONTROL.
           SELECT F ASSIGN TO "f.dat" ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED
               RECORD KEY IS R-KEY
               COLLATING SEQUENCE IS AL.
       DATA DIVISION.
       FILE SECTION.
       FD F.
       01 R.
          05 R-KEY PIC X(4).
          05 R-D   PIC X(4).
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN. STOP RUN.
